title: Per-model quantization defaults and CI calibration workflow for FP8/INT8
creator: Ayesha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams need reliable per-model defaults for quantization (FP8/INT8) exposed in the model catalog. Current one-size-fits-all recommendations cause either unnecessary accuracy regressions or missed cost savings. Goal: produce per-model default profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with automated calibration and validation pipelines, plus guardrails and CI gating so catalog entries are safe for rollout.

Proposed solution:
- Define three default profiles per model (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with explicit tokenization/sequence assumptions and kernel compatibility notes.
- Implement a calibration runner that: 1) pulls model weights, 2) runs representative calibration dataset, 3) outputs quantization parameters, 4) runs an accuracy validation suite (QA prompts + eval metrics).
- Store calibration artifacts and a small metrics summary in the catalog entry (calibration_date, dataset_hash, top-3 metrics).
- Add a CI job that rejects catalog updates if accuracy drop > threshold or if validation fails across all profiles. CI should allow manual override with audit log and required approvals.
- Provide guardrail logic for runtime: if live inference detects drift beyond specified delta from calibration baseline, automatically fallback to a higher-precision variant and create an alert.

Important constraints: calibration must run in a sandboxed infra (dedicated GPU pool), keep sample datasets <5GB per model, and produce deterministic outputs for reproducibility. For large models (>70B) default to conservative profile until we have sufficient telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog can show three recommended profiles per model with metadata fields: profile_name, expected_token_speed_pct, estimated_cost_pct, calibration_date, dataset_hash
Calibration runner produces artifacts and a JSON metrics summary stored alongside model entry
Validation suite runs automated checks (perplexity delta, task-specific metrics) and CI blocks catalog merge on high regression unless an audit-approved override is attached
Runtime guardrail can trigger automatic fallback to stored higher-precision variant and create an incident ticket with model+profile context
Documentation (Confluence) and a catalog UI stub exist for PM/Designer review
tasks: Design JSON schema additions for model catalog entries (fields + example)
Implement calibration runner prototype (calibrate + emit quant params + metrics)
Create accuracy validation harness (QA prompts, eval scripts) and baseline datasets
Add CI gating job and policy for catalog PRs
Wire runtime guardrail to fallback policy and alerting
Write docs and internal onboarding guide; update catalog UI to show profiles
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ayesha Khan: Kickoff — scoped initial MVP to support FP8 and INT8 for open models in the catalog. Prioritize smaller (<20B) models for automated calibration in MVP.

2025-02-14 - Marco Liu: Prototype calibration runner completed on resnet-style quant harness (proof of concept). Results: FP8 aggressive profile produced ~6% task-specific metric degradation on our NLU eval set for model X; conservative profile stayed within 1.2%.
2025-02-16 - PM (Sofia Ramirez): Please add acceptance criteria that requires storing dataset hashes and a short human-readable justification for any manual override in catalog PRs.

2025-02-18 - Eng review (Ravi Patel): Flagging dependency on ENG-9274 (catalog quant recommendations work). We should align field names to avoid duplication. Also noted runtime fallback requires a small change in the routing policy (runtime-1.18).

2025-02-20 - Marco Liu: CI job draft pushed: github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/PR/248 — includes a validator that runs the calibration binary in a cached sandbox. Needs perf testing and a security review for artifact storage.
notes: We will start with synthetic and curated representative datasets for each model family; later invite customers to opt-in to shared calibration telemetry. Keep manual override audit trail in catalog change logs. For large models, prefer manual gating and slower rollouts.
